case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Hem Raj
respondent:
Hem Raj
Supreme Court of India

14  May  1999
Cr. Appeal No. 190 of 1991
The Judgment was delivered by: G. T. NANAVATI, J.
1.  The State has filed this appeal against the judgment of the High Court in Criminal Appeal No. 2903 of 1978 whereby it allowed the appeal of the respondents, set aside their conviction and acquitted them.
2. facts: On 25.5.1975, sometime between 9 and 10 a.m., an exchange of words took place between Champa (the deceased) and Babu Lal, the brother of the three accused (the respondents herein) in respect of the manner in which his cattle were taken by Babu Lal from near the house of Champa.
The protested why their brother was abused by Champa. All the three then assaulted Champa and gave one blow each as a result of which Champa received injuries on her head and ultimately died.
It was also the prosecution case that Champa's husband Bachey Lal in order to save Champa had also thrown a stick towards them as a result one of them was injured.
petitioner_arguments: The High Court has committed an error of law in acquitting the accused mainly on the ground that they had no intention to kill Champa.

Even if the finding of the High Court that the quarrel between Champa and accused took place all of a sudden is accepted, they ought to have been convicted under Section 304 (Part I) of the Indian Penal Code.
respondent_arguments: The applicants are entitled to the benefit of doubt.
The evidence of the three eye witnesses has stated that the incident had taken place somewhere between 8 and 10 a.m.
It is difficult to appreciate how this evidence can be said to be inconsistent.
court_reasoning: All the three eye witnesses have stated that the incident had taken place somewhere between 8 and 10 a.m. It is difficult to appreciate how this evidence can be said to be inconsistent.
The evidence further disclose that after initial exchange of words with Champa Jodhey Lal gave a stick blow on the head of Champa as a result of which she fell down.
Jhajhan Lal (P.W.5) merely stated that Jodhey Lal assaulted Champa. He has not stated that Bhim Sen had also given blows to Champa and had injured her.
holding: The appeal is partly allowed, the judgment and order passed by the High Court in respect of Jodhey lal is set aside and restored the judgment and order passed against him by the trial Court.
Jodhey lal is ordered to surrender to custody in order to serve out the remaining part of the sentence.
The acquittal of respondents Hem Raj and Bhim Sen is confirmed and to that extent the said appeal is dismissed.
